messages.author: 11a40d58d6ce1105
messages.subject: inla memory issue?
parts:
Hi help!
 
I am running the spde model with a larger data set which has about  81809 observations. The mesh I generated has 10211 triangles and n.spde = 5247. I also want to predict this on other 81809 locations.. 
what I used is jointly estimation and prediction with inla.stack  .. 

res <- inla(resp ~ -1 + f(id, model=spde1),
  data=inla.stack.data(st.full),
  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(st.full), compute=TRUE))

It took nearly all the memory about 7~8GB overnight to run but not finished before I killed the job .. Then I searche a little bit and found some instructions on this and tried this first 

res_start <- inla(resp ~ -1 + f(id, model=spde1),
  data=inla.stack.data(st.full),
  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(st.full), compute=TRUE),
  control.inla = list(diagonal = 1000, strategy = "gaussian", int.strategy = "eb"))

res <- inla(resp ~ -1 + f(id, model=spde1),
  data=inla.stack.data(st.full),
  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(st.full), compute=TRUE),
  control.mode = list(result = res_start, restart = TRUE))

For the starting value run with diagonal = 1000, it took a few memory and was really fast with 1~2 mins and .. but when I called the second, it took again nearly all the memory ... and I killed it to let my computer rest .. 
 
I saw Finn said that he tried even larger data set with a lot of memory .. I wonder if that is the issue of memory ? how can I deal with this? Thanks a lot!
 
Best,
Xiao

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla memory issue?
parts:
On 28/11/13 11:57, xiao guo wrote:
> Hi help!
> I am running the spde model with a larger data set which has about
> 81809 observations. The mesh I generated has 10211 triangles and
> n.spde = 5247. I also want to predict this on other 81809 locations..
> what I used is jointly estimation and prediction with inla.stack ..

Yes, the "easiest" solution is to add more memory...
The other option is the one you tried, with two inla calls,
but that can still need a lot of memory for the prediction run of inla.
You can try to split that into several inla-calls (with only some of the
predictions in each call), so that each one is small enough.

Finn

> data=inla.stack.data(st.full),
> control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(st.full), compute=TRUE))

On 28 November 2013 13:04, Finn Lindgren <finn.l...@gmail.com> wrote:

I am running the spde model with a larger data set which has about

Yes, the "easiest" solution is to add more memory...
The other option is the one you tried, with two inla calls,
but that can still need a lot of memory for the prediction run of inla.
You can try to split that into several inla-calls (with only some of the predictions in each call), so that each one is small enough.

Finn

I saw Finn said that he tried even larger data set with a lot of memory

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla memory issue?
parts:
Using metres as unit for regions of multikilometre regions usually leads to numerical issues.  It's typically more robust to use km as the spatial unit instead, and the defaults in inla are adapted to data and effects on the size order "1". In any case, you need to be careful when constructing the mesh, so that e.g. max.edge is specified in the correct units.  Rescaling space is simply a change of units, and the apart from the relation to the scale of the prior distributions it should have no effect othe results, when interpreted in the correct units.  1000 metres is always 1 km.

Finn

Yes, the "easiest" solution is to add more memory...
The other option is the one you tried, with two inla calls,
but that can still need a lot of memory for the prediction run of inla.
You can try to split that into several inla-calls (with only some of the predictions in each call), so that each one is small enough.
